title: Drain Of Wealth Theory
definition: The Drain of Wealth Theory refers to the systematic transfer of India's wealth, resources, and capital to Britain without any adequate economic, commercial, or material return, which formed the core mechanism of British colonial exploitation.
importanceInUpsc: This topic is foundational for Modern Indian History in UPSC CSE. It frequently appears in Prelims regarding pioneering economists (Dadabhai Naoroji, R.C. Dutt) and literary works, and is indispensable for Mains (GS-1 Modern History, GS-3 Indian Economy) to analyze the deindustrialization of India and the impoverishment of the peasantry.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Drain Of Wealth Theory.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of British economic policies
